claims.text: Cu is a non-rare-earth FCC-stabilizing element suitable for addition to NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys.
Adding approximately 3–5 atomic % Cu and applying controlled annealing enhances chemical and magnetic homogeneity.
Improved homogeneity narrows the distribution of local magnetic exchange interactions.
A narrower distribution of exchange interactions sharpens the second-order magnetic phase transition.
Sharpening the magnetic transition increases magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
The Cu-addition and annealing treatment maintains rapid heat exchange and mechanical stability.
The initial NiFeCoCr-based alloy has a broad distribution of local exchange interactions and modest magnetocaloric performance.
Controlled annealing can homogenize the microstructure without compromising phase stability.
The relevant operating regime is near room temperature, around 1 T, and within a second-order magnetic transition.
Cu homogenizes the local atomic environment in the alloy.
Narrowing the spread of exchange interactions produces a more abrupt and nearly reversible magnetic transition.
The refined magnetic transition enhances magnetic entropy change.
The Cu-doped and annealed alloy will have a sharper and higher magnetic entropy-change response at low fields than the undoped baseline.
The Cu-doped and annealed alloy will show less magnetic hysteresis than the undoped baseline.
The Cu-doped and annealed alloy will maintain or improve thermal and mechanical properties relative to the baseline.
The undoped baseline has a less sharply defined magnetic transition, a lower magnetocaloric effect, and higher hysteresis because its exchange interactions are more broadly distributed.
The proposed mechanism applies generally to rare-earth-free, transition-metal-based high-entropy alloys processed by controlled annealing and operated near room temperature at low to moderate fields.
X-ray diffraction FWHM analysis and TEM can confirm a narrower distribution of local magnetic exchange interactions.
